blocks.content: Lakshadweep's tourism circuit is compact but distinctive, built entirely around its lagoons, beaches and marine environment — this chapter catalogues the key islands and attractions by name.

cells: UT capital; known for its lagoon, the Ujra Mosque, and the Marine Aquarium; serves as the main administrative and transit hub
Location of Lakshadweep's only airport; known for its striking lagoon and as the main air gateway for tourists

An uninhabited island long developed specifically for tourism (resort-based), historically one of Lakshadweep's best-known destinations for both domestic and international visitors, particularly popular for diving and snorkelling
Known for water sports and diving facilities; part of the Amindivi group
Known for its scenic lagoon and traditional Lakshadweep coir/handicraft production
Southernmost island, culturally distinct (Chapter 6); known for its lighthouse (one of the oldest in the region), tuna canning facility, and traditional 'Lava' dance performances
Largest island by area; historically significant as an early centre of Islamic scholarship in the archipelago

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Bangaram Island — uninhabited but resort-developed — is historically one of Lakshadweep's most internationally recognised tourism destinations, a useful fact to distinguish from Kavaratti (the administrative capital) and Agatti (the air-transit gateway), since all three are frequently tested together.

items: Scuba diving and snorkelling are the islands' flagship tourism activities, given the exceptional water clarity and coral-reef biodiversity (Chapter 8), with Bangaram, Kadmat and Agatti among the most developed diving destinations.
Lagoon-based water sports (kayaking, glass-bottom boat rides, and similar activities) are widely available across the inhabited tourist-accessible islands.

Given the territory's historically strict permit-based access system (Chapter 5), tourism has traditionally been smaller-scale and more tightly managed than comparable tropical-island destinations elsewhere in the world — a policy contrast increasingly discussed in the context of the post-2024 tourism-growth push.
Kavaratti = UT capital; Agatti = air gateway (only airport); Bangaram = flagship resort/diving island.
Minicoy: distinct culture, notable lighthouse, tuna canning facility.
Andrott = largest island by area, historic centre of Islamic scholarship.
Scuba diving/snorkelling are the flagship tourism activities, given exceptional reef biodiversity and water clarity.
